item.title: Top NW Florida volleyball seniors compete in all-star game tonight at PSC
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The best high school volleyball talent from Escambia, Santa Rosa and Okaloosa counties will take the court Thursday evening for the annual High School All-Star Volleyball Game, hosted by Pensacola Sports. The match tips off at 6:30 p.m. at Hartsell Arena on the Pensacola State College campus. Senior athletes selected by their coaches will compete…
item.content:encoded:
The best high school volleyball talent from Escambia, Santa Rosa and Okaloosa counties will take the court Thursday evening for the annual High School All-Star Volleyball Game, hosted by Pensacola Sports.

The match tips off at 6:30 p.m. at Hartsell Arena on the Pensacola State College campus. Senior athletes selected by their coaches will compete in an East-West matchup, with rosters drawn from standout performers across the three-county region. After the game, a recognition ceremony will honor the athletes with Most Valuable Player awards from each team.

"The High School All-Star Volleyball Game is about recognizing the talent, dedication and hard work these athletes have shown throughout their high school careers," Jason Libbert, president and CEO of Pensacola Sports, said in a statement. "It's an opportunity to bring the best players in the area together for one final matchup, celebrate their achievements and give fans a chance to see some outstanding volleyball."

Admission is $10 for adults and $5 for students; children 5 and under are free. Tickets are available at the door or in advance through GoFan via PensacolaSports.org. The event is open to the public, and media coverage is encouraged.

Normal business hours resume Monday, November 30. Residents needing medical attention during the closure should dial 911 for emergencies. The health department's reminder comes as the…
item.content:encoded:
Florida Department of Health offices serving Santa Rosa County will close starting Wednesday, November 25, through Friday, November 27, for the Thanksgiving holiday. Normal business hours resume Monday, November 30.

Residents needing medical attention during the closure should dial 911 for emergencies. The health department's reminder comes as the region prepares for the holiday travel and gathering season.

For non-emergency health services, residents can wait until offices reopen the following Monday or contact the department through its website at FloridaHealth.gov.

item.title: Fill the Mayflower Food Drive Returns Friday to Fight Hunger
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The annual Fill the Mayflower Food Drive returns this Friday, November 20, to combat local hunger with the help of community donations at Cordova Mall. Presented by Coastal Moving & Storage and benefiting Manna Food Bank, the drive will operate from 5:00 AM to 6:00 PM at Cordova Mall, 5100 N. 9th Ave., between BJ's Restaurant & Brewhouse and…
item.content:encoded:
The annual Fill the Mayflower Food Drive returns this Friday, November 20, to combat local hunger with the help of community donations at Cordova Mall.

Presented by Coastal Moving & Storage and benefiting Manna Food Bank, the drive will operate from 5:00 AM to 6:00 PM at Cordova Mall, 5100 N. 9th Ave., between BJ's Restaurant & Brewhouse and Regions Bank. The public is encouraged to donate nutritious, non-perishable food items and monetary gifts to support food-insecure neighbors throughout Northwest Florida.

Media support is from NewsRadio 92.3 and Cat Country 98.7. Listen to the stations for more details.

Volunteers will collect donations directly from vehicles at the Mayflower truck, making the process convenient for supporters. "Cash, checks, and credit/debit cards will be accepted, too," organizers noted. Monetary donations have immediate impact—just $25 provides food for a child in need for five days, while $50 supplies thirty healthy meals for a senior citizen.

Manna Food Bank has identified specific items currently in high demand. "Canned Fruit in 100% Juice (20 oz. or less)" ranks as the most needed item, followed by canned mixed vegetables, tuna or chicken, microwaveable meals, oatmeal boxes, and peanut butter.

While all non-perishable donations are welcomed, Manna cannot accept alcoholic beverages, homemade items, non-commercial canned goods, perishable items, opened food, or rusty or unlabeled cans to ensure food safety.

Those unable to attend in person can still contribute. "Every can and dollar stays in our community," organizers emphasized, encouraging online donations at www.mannahelps.org/donate/money/. Donors can designate contributions "In Honor Of" the Fill the Mayflower Food Drive.

Manna Food Bank served 71,005 individuals in 2025, yet demand continues to grow. The food drive, made possible by Coastal Moving & Storage and media partners including Cat Country 98.7, NewsRadio 92.3, WEAR ABC 3 News, and Cordova Mall, represents a critical community effort.

"Together, we fill more than a truck. We fill hearts, homes, and holiday tables," organizers stated.

item.title: Professional Soccer, Hard Rock Hotel Among Plans Under Review for Pensacola's Maritime Park
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. — The future of Pensacola's Community Maritime Park could include professional soccer, additional events at Blue Wahoos Stadium and new development around the waterfront. City officials are preparing a December presentation to the Pensacola City Council examining several projects that could reshape how the property is used. One…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. — The future of Pensacola's Community Maritime Park could include professional soccer, additional events at Blue Wahoos Stadium and new development around the waterfront.

City officials are preparing a December presentation to the Pensacola City Council examining several projects that could reshape how the property is used.

One possibility involves converting Blue Wahoos Stadium into a multipurpose venue capable of accommodating professional soccer in addition to baseball.

The city is exploring what modifications would be required and how much those improvements might cost.

The presentation is also expected to include an update on the proposed Hard Rock hotel development and its anticipated timeline.

A third issue involves upcoming Major League Baseball facility requirements that could require changes to the city-owned stadium.

Officials say a Major League Baseball representative may participate in the December discussion.

Financing will be a central consideration.

Mayor D.C. Reeves has suggested that future development on currently vacant Maritime Park parcels could help offset the cost of stadium improvements.

Additional restaurants, retail space or other development could generate lease revenue and property taxes while benefiting from more events at the stadium.

However, officials caution that the concept remains under study.

No final stadium expansion plan, financing arrangement or construction schedule has been approved.

The December City Council discussion is expected to provide a clearer picture of the options under consideration.

item.title: Florida Set to Break Execution Record With 20th Death Sentence Carried Out This Year
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: RAIFORD, Fla. — Florida is scheduled to establish a new single-year execution record Thursday evening with the planned lethal injection of 71-year-old Thomas Mitchell Overton. Overton is scheduled to be executed at 6 p.m. at Florida State Prison in Raiford. He was convicted of murdering Michael and Susan MacIvor during a 1991 home invasion in the…
item.content:encoded:
RAIFORD, Fla. — Florida is scheduled to establish a new single-year execution record Thursday evening with the planned lethal injection of 71-year-old Thomas Mitchell Overton.

Overton is scheduled to be executed at 6 p.m. at Florida State Prison in Raiford.

He was convicted of murdering Michael and Susan MacIvor during a 1991 home invasion in the Florida Keys.

Susan MacIvor was eight months pregnant when she was killed.

The couple was discovered dead inside their Tavernier home on August 22, 1991. Autopsies determined both victims had been strangled.

Investigators collected DNA evidence from the crime scene but initially could not identify a suspect.

The investigation advanced after Overton was arrested on an unrelated burglary charge in 1996. Authorities said DNA collected from him matched evidence from the MacIvors' home.

Overton was convicted in 1999 and sentenced to death. His attorneys have challenged the evidence used to secure the conviction.

Thursday's execution would be Florida's 20th of 2026, surpassing the 19 executions carried out in 2025.

Florida has conducted more than half of the executions in the United States this year.

Governor Ron DeSantis, who leaves office in January, has signed additional death warrants, with two more executions scheduled for December.

Appeals in Overton's case were pending ahead of Thursday's scheduled execution.

item.title: UWF gets $500K state grant for free AI, cybersecurity training across Florida
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The University of West Florida's Center for Cybersecurity and AI has landed a nearly half-million-dollar state grant to launch Future-Ready Florida, a new statewide program offering free online training in artificial intelligence and cybersecurity. Funded by the Florida Legislature through the Florida Department of Management Services, the…
item.content:encoded:
The University of West Florida's Center for Cybersecurity and AI has landed a nearly half-million-dollar state grant to launch Future-Ready Florida, a new statewide program offering free online training in artificial intelligence and cybersecurity.

Funded by the Florida Legislature through the Florida Department of Management Services, the initiative will provide seven online courses to at least 350 eligible participants across the state. The program is designed to equip Florida residents and public-sector workers with skills in two rapidly growing technology fields while bolstering the state's economic competitiveness.

Participants can choose from three flexible training formats: self-paced foundational courses, two-week technical courses, and nine-week industry certification preparation courses. The offerings focus on two main tracks—AI Readiness and Innovation, and Cyber Defense and Operations. Successful participants can earn UWF digital badges and certificates of completion, with eligible enrollees also receiving industry certification exam prep and vouchers.

The program is open to Florida residents and state and local government employees, including public school staff. Each participant may enroll in one course to maximize access opportunities statewide. UWF President Manny Diaz Jr. called the investment an opportunity to extend the university's expertise beyond campus and strengthen Florida's talent pool in emerging technologies. For course schedules, eligibility details, and registration, visit uwf.edu/futurereadyfl.

item.title: Pensacola Considers Public Safety Cuts and City Property Review as Budget Pressure Mounts
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. — Police and fire services could be affected as Pensacola prepares for millions of dollars in lost property-tax revenue following the passage of Florida's Amendment 3. Mayor D.C. Reeves says the city is reviewing spending across its departments, including public safety, as officials prepare for the financial impact of the…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. — Police and fire services could be affected as Pensacola prepares for millions of dollars in lost property-tax revenue following the passage of Florida's Amendment 3.

Mayor D.C. Reeves says the city is reviewing spending across its departments, including public safety, as officials prepare for the financial impact of the voter-approved changes.

The administration estimates Pensacola could lose approximately $4.2 million in revenue next year, with that figure increasing to $7.2 million the following year, plus additional losses to the Community Redevelopment Agency.

Reeves acknowledged that police and fire services represent a substantial part of the city's budget and cannot automatically be excluded from the discussion.

The city is also examining its property holdings, including buildings that may no longer be in use, as officials consider ways to reduce expenses or generate revenue.

No property sales or service reductions have been approved.

Department directors are expected to submit potential cost-saving proposals, which the administration will review before making recommendations.

Adding to the financial pressure is Hurricane Isaias. The city is tracking more than $10 million in storm-related expenses while working through the federal reimbursement process.

Reeves says the goal is to respect voters' decision to reduce property taxes while limiting disruptions to essential city services.

The case was highlighted on social media, drawing attention to what authorities describe as a significant theft of federal tax revenue. Details on how the alleged theft occurred and the specific charges filed were not immediately available.

The investigation underscores ongoing federal efforts to pursue cases involving the misappropriation of IRS funds and assets.

item.title: Defense contractor Birdon expands Port of Pensacola footprint for $275M shipbuilding facility

The expansion is part of Birdon's broader effort to establish a major manufacturing and shipbuilding operation in the region. The facility is…
item.content:encoded:
Defense contractor Birdon is expanding its operational footprint at the Port of Pensacola, increasing its lease area from 10 acres to 16 acres to support a $275 million shipbuilding facility in development.

The expansion is part of Birdon's broader effort to establish a major manufacturing and shipbuilding operation in the region. The facility is expected to bring approximately 2,000 jobs to the Pensacola area once fully operational, representing a significant economic development win for Escambia County and the port authority.

The Port of Pensacola has increasingly positioned itself as a hub for defense contracting and maritime manufacturing. Birdon's expansion signals growing confidence in the port's infrastructure and workforce capacity to support large-scale naval and defense shipbuilding operations.

The theft was captured on cellphone video, which showed the woman taking money from the man during the fight. The case was prosecuted in what appears to be a plea agreement that reduced the original charge.

Details about the specific sentencing length and the exact location of the Century store were not immediately provided in available reports.

A grand opening date for the Cantonment store has not yet been announced.

item.title: AAA releases e-bike buying guide ahead of holiday season
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: As electric bikes and scooters climb holiday wish lists, AAA is urging buyers to look beyond price tags and flashy features. The organization released a free E-Bike Gift Guide on Thursday to help families navigate what can be a confusing market with varying speeds, power levels, and legal restrictions. According to AAA spokesman Mark Jenkins, the…
item.content:encoded:
As electric bikes and scooters climb holiday wish lists, AAA is urging buyers to look beyond price tags and flashy features. The organization released a free E-Bike Gift Guide on Thursday to help families navigate what can be a confusing market with varying speeds, power levels, and legal restrictions.

According to AAA spokesman Mark Jenkins, the guide addresses a key safety concern: "A device that's too fast or powerful for the rider can quickly become a safety risk." The two-page resource walks shoppers through device comparisons, legal classifications, battery systems, and brake quality — plus red flags like unclear top speeds or devices marketed as "unlockable" beyond advertised limits.

One critical distinction the guide highlights is the difference between e-bikes and e-motos. While traditional e-bikes assist riders up to 20 or 28 mph depending on their class, e-motos can exceed those speeds with motorcycle-style controls. Some higher-powered devices may not be street-legal without registration, insurance, and licensing — requirements that vary by state and community.

Helmet protection matters too, AAA says. The guide recommends matching helmet standards to device capability: CPSC-certified bicycle helmets for traditional bikes, NTA 8776 helmets for higher-speed e-bikes, and DOT-compliant motorcycle helmets for devices capable of motorcycle-level speeds. The free E-Bike Gift Guide is available at sm.aaa/EBikeGiftGuide.

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County is moving forward with a safety upgrade at Highway 29 and County Road 196, where a 17-year-old was killed in a crash. Construction is now underway on a new traffic signal at the intersection, according to WKRG-TV 5.

The project represents an effort to improve traffic control at a location that has been the site of a fatal accident. Installation of the stoplight is expected to help manage vehicle flow and reduce collision risks at the busy intersection.

Details on the project timeline and completion date were not immediately available.
